audition.title: Our Banking Client — technology talk audition
audition.text:
Here's the problem. Seventy-five people are testing, but they're waiting on the same few environments. Backend services aren't virtualized. The vendor gives us limited test slots. The bottleneck is test capacity.

So let's change the system.

Spin up an isolated test environment. Model the vendor service. Now we can replay a timeout, a duplicate callback, or a failed retry, whenever we need to.

Then bring in AI. Copilot helps engineers draft tests. An agent can help explain CI failures and pull the evidence together. Engineers review the code and make the release decision.

Here's our banking test scenario. The payment times out. The customer hits retry. We need to prove that one payment creates one debit.

That's the pilot: repeatable tests, faster feedback, and evidence we can trust. Measure modernization first. Then measure what AI adds.

slide-18.title: Before / after: the shared QE architecture
slide-18.text:
Start on the left. Our Banking Client has seventy-five offshore QA staff, including forty-five manual and domain testers. They share a few test environments. Backend services are not virtualized, and vendor test slots limit parallel runs. Manual execution, reruns and evidence collection add coordination work.

The proposed target is on the right. Squads reuse supported QE services: controlled test data, isolated runs, virtualized dependencies and retained evidence. This foundation lets teams repeat service tests without waiting for every vendor slot.

AI adds assistance with test preparation and interpretation. People still approve expected behavior, review generated changes and make release decisions. Real provider checks remain necessary.

The next slide shows how we will judge this architecture through quality outcomes, alongside effort.

slide-19.title: Outcomes beyond hours
slide-19.text:
Success needs evidence beyond hours saved. We propose three primary measures for the banking pilot.

First, detect every approved critical payment fault that we deliberately introduce. Second, exercise every critical scenario with reviewed assertions and a valid result. Third, make each release decision traceable to its requirements, build, test data and raw results.

Then check the foundation: can the team repeat runs reliably, validate agreed behaviors against the real provider, and help a second squad run independently?

These measures have no recorded baseline or after result yet. We will compare today's workflow, modernized QE, and AI assistance on that foundation. Fewer escaped defects and emergency fixes are business aims to validate across releases. A complete evidence pack can still recommend stopping a release.

slide-26.title: Integration adapters have explicit contracts
slide-26.text:
Read this slide as four owned integration contracts.

The context adapter packages versioned stories, API contracts and test revisions. Unresolved behavior blocks approval of the affected cases.

The model adapter accepts that bundle and its configuration, then returns a proposed patch. A timeout or quota failure produces no candidate. Retries are bounded and recorded.

The runner accepts an approved test commit and run manifest. It executes deterministic checks, preserves the original exit status, retains raw evidence, and then cleans up the environment.

The evidence adapter indexes those artifacts using traceable run identifiers. Missing joins remain unknown. AI can draft a read-only explanation; it cannot turn missing or failed evidence into a pass.

These contracts connect the controlled execution environment to traceable API test evidence.

slide-27.title: Before / after: the API test architecture
slide-27.text:
On the left, manual API and interface runs compete for shared backend services, PostgreSQL accounts and limited vendor test slots. There is no backend service virtualization. Engineers collect logs and screenshots manually.

On the right, an approved test commit enters a pinned CI runner. The pilot provisions a payment service and datastore for each run, resets synthetic balances, and uses versioned WireMock behavior to reproduce provider faults.

JUnit and REST Assured check the transfer, journal and balances. An idempotency scenario verifies that a retried payment creates one transfer and one balanced journal. Raw assertions, application logs and run identifiers survive cleanup.

AI assists drafting and evidence interpretation under review. Isolated execution and controlled dependencies come from QE modernization. Real provider and settlement checks remain separate gates.
